item.title: Iran Crisis 2026 - Day 39 Brief
item.description:
Day 39 of the Iran-2026 conflict is defined by an unprecedented escalation in coercive diplomacy and sustained kinetic pressure, with the 8 PM ET deadline now approximately 10 hours away as of this morning. An intensive overnight US-Israeli strike wave hit Tehran (including a destroyed synagogue with 15 killed), Karaj, Najafabad, and Yazd. Mehrabad Airport in Tehran was confirmed in flames. In the early hours, Israel bombed key rail sections and bridges to disrupt IRGC weapons movement, and issued a Farsi-language warning to Iranians to avoid rail travel until 21:00. The midday strike wave hit Khorramabad Airport and a Space Research Center in Tehran. US strikes then hit Iran's Kharg Island export terminal — the country's largest — triggering a 2% spike in US oil prices. The IRGC responded by warning that 'restraint is over' and threatening years of regional oil and gas disruption.
As the deadline approaches, President Trump has escalated his language dramatically: after warning that every bridge and power plant would be destroyed within four hours, he warned on April 7 that 'a whole civilization will die tonight' if Iran does not open Hormuz. Vice President Vance separately stated the US has 'tools in our toolkit that we so far haven't decided to use' on Iran. Mediators Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey pushed a 45-day ceasefire framework, but Iran formally rejected it — refusing to open Hormuz even temporarily. Netanyahu reportedly urged Trump not to proceed with a ceasefire at this stage.
On the kinetic side: the IDF detected Iranian ballistic missile fire this morning (likely intercepted, sirens in south Israel); Hezbollah simultaneously fired rockets at northern Israel; and a gunfight erupted at the Israeli consulate in Istanbul (1 attacker killed, 2 police injured). All three incidents suggest the Axis of Resistance remains active and coordinated heading into the deadline.

item.title: Iran Crisis 2026 - Day 37 Brief
item.description:
Day 37 is defined by two parallel threads: the dramatic completion of the US F-15E crew rescue deep inside Iran, and the continued escalation of the Hormuz ultimatum crisis. CENTCOM confirmed that both F-15E crewmembers have been recovered after Iran shot down their aircraft on April 2. The weapons system officer, who evaded capture for 36 hours, was secured by US special operations forces in a complex mission involving over 150 aircraft, Israeli Shaldag and Sayeret Matkal assistance, and CIA deception operations. US forces established a makeshift airstrip inside Iran, destroyed two transport aircraft and MH-6 Little Birds they could not extract, and spent seven hours over Iranian territory in the second raid alone. Trump called it 'one of the most complex search-and-rescue missions ever.'
Simultaneously, the Hormuz ultimatum entered its most critical phase. Trump extended the deadline for Iran to cease shipping attacks to 8:00 PM ET on April 7, threatening strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure and bridges if the deadline passes. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei rejected the ultimatum, declaring Iran would continue threatening shipping in the Strait. Pakistan proposed a 45-day ceasefire framework; Iranian FM Araghchi held mediation talks with Pakistani FM Ishaq Dar, but Iran pushed for broader maximalist terms rather than accepting the proposal.
Iran continued its Gulf state strike campaign with an altered package emphasizing cruise missiles — four at Kuwait, two at Qatar, one each at UAE and Saudi Arabia. Kuwaiti power generation and water desalination facilities were hit, as were Bahrain's GPIC petrochemical units and BAPCO storage tanks, and a Borouge petrochemicals plant in the UAE. Iranian missiles struck inside Israel, including a residential building hit directly in Haifa.
Hezbollah escalated with its first anti-ship cruise missile attack against an Israeli warship 68 nautical miles off the Lebanese coast, estimated by Israel to have caused damage. Hezbollah also claimed 40 attacks in a 24-hour period against Israeli targets in southern Lebanon and northern Israel, with rockets injuring six in Deir al Asad and a drone striking a home in Shomrat. The IDF assessed Hezbollah can sustain 200 launches per day for five additional months.
The combined US-Israeli decapitation campaign continued with the killing of IRGC Brigadier General Mostafa Azizi (IRGC Navy 3rd Imam Hossein Naval District), Mohammad Reza Ashrafi Ghahi (head of commerce at IRGC Oil Headquarters), and Artesh Air Defense Academy Commander Brigadier General Masoud Zare. Missile launchers were struck in Kamyaran and Farashband, and the IRGC Ground Forces 14th Imam Hossein Division headquarters in Esfahan was hit. Bank Sepah suffered a major computer network disruption preventing IRGC salary payments.
Escalation: 93/100

item.title: Iran Crisis 2026 - Day 35 Brief
item.description:
Day 35 of the Iran crisis opened with Iran's most expansive Gulf-state strike campaign to date, targeting critical infrastructure across Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain, and triggering Saudi interceptor responses overnight. Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery in Kuwait — already struck twice in two weeks — was hit a third time, sparking fires that Kuwait Petroleum Corp confirmed would take days to contain. Iran also struck the Shuaiba desalination plant, inflicting material damage to water and power infrastructure serving Kuwait City. In the UAE, Iranian drone debris ignited fires at the Habshan gas facility and killed a Bangladeshi farmworker in Ajban — the first civilian fatality from falling debris in the Gulf. Explosions were reported in central Isfahan. Iran's IRGC claimed it shot down a second US F-35 over central Iran, with 'low chances of pilot survival', though the US did not confirm the loss.

Iran also retains thousands of one-way drones and a large share of its coastal cruise missiles. The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier departed Croatia after fire repairs, heading back toward the Arabian Sea.

Day 13 - Daily Intelligence Brief

Escalation: 95/100

Summary

Day 13 of the US-Israel war on Iran. Overnight saw IRGC-Hezbollah execute their first declared joint operation against Israel. Iran expanded Gulf infrastructure attacks — drone struck building near Dubai Creek Harbour, oil tanks ablaze near Bahrain airport, explosive boats hit Iraqi tankers shutting all oil terminals. Saudi Arabia and Kuwait intercepted Iranian drones targeting Riyadh embassy district. IDF launched wide-scale strikes across Lebanon and drone attacks on Tehran. Brent crude topped $100/bbl. IEA coordinated record 400M barrel strategic reserve release. UNSC demanded Iran halt Gulf attacks. Iran threatened to target US tech company offices.

Key Facts

  • IDF struck Taleghan nuclear compound near Tehran — AMAD Project weapons development site
  • IRGC and Hezbollah declared first joint operation — coordinated missile and rocket fire at Israel
  • Iran fired 4th ballistic missile salvo at Israel since midnight — sirens across Jerusalem
  • Hezbollah rocket destroyed home in Moshav Haniel, central Israel — safe room saved occupants
  • Iranian drones damaged Kuwait International Airport — material damage, no casualties
  • Iranian attack caused major fire at oil tanks near Bahrain International Airport
  • Iranian explosive boats attacked Iraqi fuel tankers — 1 killed, Iraq shut all oil terminals
  • Saudi Arabia downed drone near Riyadh embassy district; intercepted Shaybah drones 3x
  • IDF wide-scale strikes on Lebanon + Tehran; killed 7 in Beirut seafront strike
  • US CENTCOM destroyed Iranian aircraft at Kerman Airport — C-130, P-3, Il-76
  • Poland foiled Iranian cyberattack on national nuclear research center
  • Up to 3.2 million displaced inside Iran — UNHCR
  • Australia pulls non-essential diplomats from Israel and UAE
  • Defense Minister Katz warns: IDF told to prepare expansion into Lebanon
  • First 6 days cost US >$11B; war tracker >$17B total at ~$1B/day
  • Brent crude >$100/bbl despite IEA 400M barrel strategic reserve release

Casualties

  • US: 7 KIA, 140 wounded, 0 civilians

Economic Impact

Brent crude has surged past $100/bbl as Iran enforces a Strait of Hormuz closure strategy, with new Supreme Leader Khamenei formally codifying it as leverage. The US military admitted it cannot yet escort tankers — all assets committed to the air campaign. Iraq shut all oil terminals after Iranian explosive boats attacked two foreign tankers. The IEA coordinated a 400-million-barrel strategic reserve release across 32 countries. Pentagon briefed Congress the first six days cost $11.3 billion; total war tracker exceeds $17 billion. Iran continues exporting ~1.5M bbl/day to China despite the conflict.

    Iran continues asymmetric attacks on Gulf infrastructure. IRGC-Hezbollah joint operations become routine. Hormuz remains closed. Oil above $100. US-Israel air campaign degrades Iranian capacity but cannot stop dispersed strikes. War cost exceeds $1B/day for US.
  • Lebanon Ground Escalation (35%) - IDF launches ground operation in southern Lebanon — Katz orders preparation
    Defense Minister Katz has now explicitly warned Lebanon and instructed IDF to prepare for expansion. Golani Brigade transferred to Northern Command. Hezbollah 200-rocket barrage demonstrates continued threat. Ground operation would aim to push Hezbollah back from border but risks major casualties and deeper Iranian involvement.
  • Iranian Tempo Collapse (15%) - Air campaign degrades Iranian strike capacity — attack frequency drops
    CENTCOM destroyed Iranian aircraft at Kerman. Over 5,500 targets struck. Trump claims Iran at end of the line. But Iran still firing 4 ballistic salvos per night and hitting Gulf infrastructure across 5+ countries.
  • Diplomatic Off-Ramp (10%) - Pezeshkian 3 conditions create framework — but no active channel
    Pezeshkian outlined conditions: rights recognition, reparations, security guarantees. But Iran spurned two Witkoff ceasefire messages. Trump demands regime change. No active negotiation channel visible.
